{"number":857,"title":"Where CI time goes: fixture signing, the fleet-wide numbers, and a weekly measurement","body":"Fixes #855. The breakdown you asked for, the one real find in it, and the standing mechanism so the next answer doesn't come from a hand-run investigation.

## The breakdown

CI job ~60s: checkout 3–5s, setup-node 5s, **unit tests 48s**, conformance sweep 1–2s, the two gates ~0s. Only the test step is worth profiling.

Under CI-like conditions the suite is **146s serial across 142 files**, and the distribution is the interesting part: not a few slow tests, but **583 tests in the 200ms–1s band** — the signature of a fixed per-test cost in a shared fixture helper, which is where the find was.

## Fleet-wide: already fast, and now recorded

Measured first, since it was named the priority. What every member actually runs:

| surface | cost |
|---|---|
| `check_the_work` (Stop hook, every session) | 235ms |
| `check_the_world` (converge / CI) | ~800ms, of which **88ms is rule execution** |
| `discoverPacks` / `buildContext` | 58ms / 41ms |

37 rules, slowest `pack-discovery-entry-await` at 63ms. The rest of the ~800ms is Node startup plus the eager pack-tree import. There is nothing to win here, and members carry smaller pack sets than the canon, so they pay less. Recording the numbers is the deliverable — it stops this being re-profiled.

## The find: fixture commits were being signed

`makeRepo` pins identity and auto-gc but inherited the host's `commit.gpgsign`, so in a session with signing configured every fixture commit became a round trip to a signing service — **202ms per fixture against 38ms without**, and the local suite **71s → 52s**.

Runners have no signing configured, so **CI never paid this**. That is also the explanation for the gap in the last PR, where local showed 33% and CI 10%: the local box was dominated by a cost CI does not have. Both numbers are stated separately throughout rather than letting the flattering one stand.

It is still worth fixing — every agent session in this repo pays it, and the degraded-service failure mode is worse than slow: each commit blocks and leaks descriptors until git fails process-wide, for reasons pointing nowhere near the code under test. The test pins the **isolation**, not the speed — it forces a hostile ambient config (signing on, program `/bin/false`) and requires the fixture to build anyway, so it means the same thing on a runner. Seen failing first (`gpg failed to sign the data`).

## What this PR does *not* do any more

An earlier commit promoted that lesson into `basics/writing-tests` as a portable practice. Reviewed and reverted in the same PR: **every** caller of `makeRepo` is a Claudinite conformance-check test, there are none in `packs/` or `engine/` product code, and a member's app tests have no reason to build a git repo — the fixture is a repo only because the subject under test takes a repo as input, which is this project's business alone. The local pack's "portable candidate" marker was itself the misjudgment, inherited rather than tested.

It needs no prose home at all now: the helper pins the config and `engine-tests/helpers-git-fixtures.test.mjs` goes red if that is removed. A guarded invariant belongs on the strongest rung of the ladder, not restated as prose that every session pays for.

## A negative result, reported rather than shipped

`packs-tests/rehearsal/rehearsal.test.mjs` is 27.6s — 19% of the serial total and 4× the next file. Its 25 cases are independent, so bounded concurrency looked obvious. It moved the file 27.6s → 25s and **the whole suite not at all**: 51s in both arms, twice each. Once signing is out of the way the suite is CPU-bound on 4 cores. Reverted — complexity that buys nothing measurable doesn't ship.

## The standing mechanism

- **`ci-performance-evaluation` skill** — the method, in the order the steps have to happen, including the two traps this investigation hit: a local profile dominated by a cost CI doesn't have, and a file-level win that vanishes at suite level. Also the reading that matters most: a test that waits is often reporting a bug, not just being slow — that reading is what found the `prework_timeout` that never killed anything.
- **`basics/ci-performance` weekly task** — measures each workflow's median over the window against the previous one, refreshes a standing tracker issue, and requests an agent **only** on a real regression (≥1.25× *and* ≥20s, with ≥3 runs each side; a quiet week costs no agent). Verdict logic is pure and tested, each guard mutated to watch it bite.

One note on that task: its precondition was first written taking `{ signals }`, and its direct-call test passed happily. Driving the real `planRun` — this repo's own rule that a task is gated twice — showed `precondition threw` on every run. Fixed, and the test now goes through `runPrecondition` so it can't re-enshrine an invented calling convention.

## Verification

1700 tests green, world sweep 0 blocking, selftest strict clean, and the new task discovered by the real scheduler scan and dispatching correctly through `planRun` on a busy week / standing down on a quiet one.","state":"open","draft":false,"merged":false,"mergeable_state":"clean","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/857","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"head":{"ref":"claude/ci-run-time-optimization-zwi9t7","sha":"a5d2f75149be8e5400f36e87d198688f5560dddf","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"ad1d8b06c1c41ea75f141f90056a7d6478835608","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"additions":567,"deletions":10,"changed_files":9,"commits":4,"created_at":"2026-08-15T10:33:10Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T22:47:11Z"}

{"number":853,"title":"Promote eight fleet lessons into the canon","body":"Growth promote, 2026-08-15. Context members read: **ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog** — their local packs' `RULES.md` prose and check modules.

Eight lessons cleared the bar. Six are folds into an existing rule (a measured sharpening of what the corpus already said); two are new bullets in a doc that owns the subject. Every one is prose — the reasons are per-row below. `Refs #852`.

| Lesson (generalized) | Origin | Landed |
|---|---|---|
| Naming a path in `node --test` is not enough — the argument must resolve to files that exist; a typo'd glob is the same zero-test green | ClaudiniteWebsite (`node-test-discovery` check) | `packs/node/RULES.md` — sharpens the test-discovery bullet |
| When you know the exact title, don't search — an MCP layer may match *semantically* and honour no qualifier, so `in:title` filters nothing; enumerate and match in-session | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — sharpens "Cap *and* qualify" |
| The per-object **field set** is the payload knob, not the page size — the same call at two page sizes returned byte-identical output | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — same section, new sub-bullet |
| A rebase that drops part of a branch must amend the commit message in the same step — under squash merge the commit body *is* `main`'s record, and a PR comment isn't carried | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — commit-layering section |
| Find an already-open issue by the **invariant identifier** the finding names, never the sentence it arrived in — every filer paraphrases the message | MissingBulbWebsite | `packs/basics/RULES.md` — extends the "open a dedicated issue unless one is already open" bullet |
| A harness wake-up needs `prompt` unless `stop: true`; a no-op flag and a `reason` don't exempt it | ClaudiniteWebsite + Sheepdog + MissingBulbWebsite (3 of 4) | `packs/basics/RULES.md` — Harness-tool contracts |
| Telling a reader to *run* something ships the literal invocation, not the filename (measured 5/5 vs 0/5 first-try) — and a rule filed where its reader never looks cannot repair a defective instruction | Sheepdog | `authoring-agent-docs` — "Shape a rule so it fires" + "Maintain it like code" |
| Seeing a figure in several search results is not evidence of who published it — snippets quote each other; attribute to the named origin | MissingBulbWebsite | `packs/product-wiki/RULES.md` |
| A dedupe search that finds nothing, on a rule naming an identifier you don't own, more likely means the mechanism **expired** than that the lesson is novel | Sheepdog | `extracting-lessons.md` — extends "Dedupe ruthlessly" |

[{"sha":"a03810950f6b73077e46fd94c18d7248c9567c72","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/a03810950f6b73077e46fd94c18d7248c9567c72","message":"The work-item queue: the whole mechanism, canon flipped

PR-1 of the tasks-dispatch migration. Work items are issues; a thin tick gives
every recurring task a standing item at its anchor and flips blocked items
ready, and any number of executors pull from the queue — evaluating the
precondition exactly once, at pickup, and rolling the item to its next anchor on
a no-go so "asked, declined, wakes at T" lives on the item rather than in a
run-ledger watermark nobody can see.

The mechanism ships behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`, which only this repo sets
to "queue"; every member keeps the slot machinery, which stays in the tree until
the fleet flip deletes it. The two are disjoint by construction — separate issue
families, separate workflows, separate janitor sweep — so the rollback is the
same config edit backwards.

- engine/scheduler/queue/: the item vocabulary, anchors, the tick's three jobs,
  the executor loop with its verified lease and post-claim re-verify, the
  janitor's four rules, the invocation call, and the create/wake levers.
- The claim arbiter is episode-scoped and ordered by comment id, the occurrence
  guard reads both created_at and closed_at, `after` compiles to a pick-time
  yield rather than a Blocked-by edge — each of these is a bug the simulator
  caught in the spec (F13, F15, F16, F18, S24) and each has a test naming it.
- Three additive task declarations: `after`, `on_interrupt`, and
  `invocation_endpoint` (a name, never a URL). The contract now also rejects a
  prework_timeout that reaches the executor's claim leash, which would livelock
  the item rather than merely duplicate a run.
- The signal collectors learn `[claudinite-work]` before any repo flips, so the
  queue's own churn never reads as repo activity to a precondition.

The endpoint map is deliberately unset: until it is configured, a hand-off
converges its item to triage naming exactly what is missing, which is the same
posture required_secrets has.

The design said "a CCR API call" and left the shape to implementation. The
routines documentation answers it, and the answer moves something: firing a
routine runs ITS stored prompt, and the `text` we send arrives wrapped in a block
explicitly labelled untrusted that a routine acts on only because its own prompt
says to.

So the payload names the item and the nonce and instructs nothing, and the
instructions live in a tracked file — queue/routine-prompt.md — pasted into the
routine. The issue-is-data posture survives the extra hop intact: behavior comes
from files under review, never from what an API caller sent.

Three corrections that a comment-shaped guess would have shipped wrong: the body
carries one freeform `text` field (structured JSON would arrive as a literal
string), the response names `claude_code_session_id`, and the endpoint is a dated
research preview whose beta header must ride every call — configurable per
endpoint, so rotating it is a config edit on one repo rather than an engine
release the fleet waits for.

idempotency key, so the agent-side lease is the mechanism that collapses a

Refs #801","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-15T10:02:53Z"}},{"sha":"f0e18dcecd2af1fc2b57c4edad935a2a1aa043ff","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/f0e18dcecd2af1fc2b57c4edad935a2a1aa043ff","message":"One call per item: the agent-side claim protocol deletes

Owner correction: the API should be called once per item. It is right, and it
removes a whole protocol rather than simplifying one.

The agent-side claim existed only because invocation was at-least-once — I
retried a call whose outcome I could not know, and a client-side timeout may
well have started a session, so two could arrive at one item and needed
arbitrating. But a retry is only safe when you know the first call did nothing,
and the timeout is exactly the case where you cannot. Declining to retry keeps
invocation at-most-once, and the lease has nothing left to collapse.

So the invoker calls once, with no `attempts` knob for anyone to raise, and
reports three outcomes instead of two. Refused (a status came back) is definite:
no session, a token or URL or routine is wrong, converge needs-human. Unanswered
is the one that matters: the item STAYS with the agent, saying so, and is settled
by a rule that already exists — a session that started converges it, one that
never did is swept by the janitor's agent leash. No re-queue that could
duplicate, no attempt counter, no bounded revert.

What survives is a check, not a claim: the session confirms the item's newest
hand-off nonce matches the fire it arrived on, and stops if it does not. One
comparison, and it still catches a replay.

The routine's stored prompt is now one line pointing at a tracked
instructions.md, so the whole of what a session does is under review — the same
rule the work item obeys. Canon's two endpoints and their token secrets are
configured.

{"number":882,"title":"Queue sessions write `claudinite-task-exec … [unknown]` — instructions.md never says what replaces the slot id","body":"Seen on the queue's first agentic run ([#867](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/867), #801 burst B3). The session printed:

```
claudinite-task-exec v1 tidy-repo/tidy-issues [unknown] success
```

The record's format is `claudinite-task-exec v1 / [] ` (`engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs`), and under slot dispatch that field carried the occurrence's identity. **The queue has no slot**, and `engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` step 5 says only *"print the `claudinite-task-exec` record"* — so the session had nothing to put there and wrote `[unknown]`, which is the reasonable guess.

What it costs: the record can no longer be tied back to the work item it describes. Under slots the field was the join key between a record and its occurrence; the queue's equivalent identity is the **issue number**, and it is being dropped on every agentic run.

Not affected: the usage fold's dedup, which keys on the full `(pack, task, slot, status)` tuple *within one capture file*. One session runs one item, so a file holds one record and a constant `[unknown]` collapses nothing that should not collapse. This is a lost join, not a miscount — worth fixing while it is one line, before every queue-mode capture in the fleet carries it.

### Fix

Have `instructions.md` name the field explicitly — the item number, `[#867]` — so a session is told rather than guessing. Check `parseTaskExecs`' pattern accepts it (the existing tests match `\[\S+\]`, which it satisfies) and add a fold test over a queue-shaped record so the format is pinned on both sides.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/882","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-15T22:47:00Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T22:47:00Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

{"number":880,"title":"Coded → declared checks: full 54-rule conversion inventory, and the 7 that are actually convertible","body":"Follow-up to #838 (question 3: "which of the remaining imperative checks could move to declarative form"). That issue asked the question; this one answers it exhaustively, rule by rule, so the conversion backlog stops being a guess.

## Corpus census (2026-08-15, `main`)

Counted by importing `discoverPacks` from `engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs` over the whole tree (pack-level `rules` + `skillChecks`), cross-checked against every tracked `declared-checks.json`:

| | coded | declared | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| canon packs (`packs/`), pack-level | 41 | 26 | 67 |
| canon packs, skill-level | 7 | 10 | 17 |
| local packs (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) | 6 | 1 | 7 |
| **total** | **54** | **37** | **91** |

Declared checks live in 12 files: 6 pack-level (`aws-sam` 2, `basics` 5, `chrome-extension-release` 5, `core` 3, `github-actions` 5, `product-wiki` 6), 5 skill-level (`google-identity` 2, `grow_with_claudinite` 1, `jwt` 2+3, `web-speech` 2), 1 local (`canon-curation` 1).

Reference point for anyone reading the numbers: the `41 checks` in the SessionStart line is the **active** set for this repo's own declaration, not the corpus; and `packs/README.md`'s hand-maintained "Hardcoded conformance checks" tally tracks only the coded half. Neither is comparable to the 91.

## Method

The dividing line is what a declaration *can* be. A declared check is data: patterns over a file set, parsed JSON/YAML field assertions, markdown-section assertions, key-value-file assertions, and reference-barrier edges — the vocabulary documented in the header of `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs`. It has no access to the conversation transcript, to git, to `.claudinite-checks.json` as a normalized *config object*, or to the discovered pack objects; and it cannot compute — no path resolution, no cross-field arithmetic, no deriving its scan set from another file's contents.

Every one of the 54 coded rule modules was read. Each is assigned exactly one primary blocker.

## A — convertible, or one named vocabulary key away (7)

This is the real backlog. Four small additive keys unlock six of them; one converts today.

| Rule | What it asserts | What is missing |
|---|---|---|
| `product-wiki-layout` (`packs/product-wiki/layout.mjs`) | the index README and the reviewed product-requirements sink exist | **Nothing — convertible today.** That half is exactly `requirePaths`. The `configGuard` half (validating the pack entry's config) stays coded; this is a split, not a move. |
| `core-declared` (`packs/core/core-declared.mjs`) | `.claudinite-checks.json`'s `packs` array names `core` | `requireValueInArray` — the exact mirror of the existing `forbidValueInArray`. Note the rule's own header: it reports, it cannot rescue (activation reads the literal declaration), so converting it changes nothing about that property. |
| `home-seeded-packs-declared` (`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/home-seeded-packs-declared.mjs`) | every `packs/*/pack.mjs` setting `seededByDefault: true` is named in the home's declaration | `requireIndexCoverage`'s exact shape, except the quantifier needs a **content** predicate — "each tracked path *whose text matches* X" alongside today's path-pattern quantifier. Also needs the comment-stripped view, which `scanIgnoringComments` already provides. |
| `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` (`packs/chrome-extension-release/privacy-permission-alignment.mjs`) | every manifest permission is disclosed in `PRIVACY.md` | Same family, values instead of paths: quantify over a parsed JSON array's *values* and require each in another file's text. `requireIndexCoverage` quantifies paths only. |
| `sudden-termination-vs-teardown` (`packs/macos/sudden-termination-vs-teardown.mjs`) | `NSSupportsSuddenTermination` is `` in a tree that has terminate-time teardown to lose | `andPreviousLineMatches` — only the negative `unlessPreviousLineMatches` exists, and the plist pairing is `…` / `` across two lines. The cross-file gate (Swift evidence of teardown) is already `relevantWhen.someTrackedFileContains`. |
| `gha/checkout-submodules` (`packs/github-actions/checkout-submodules.mjs`) | every `actions/checkout` passes `submodules: true` where `.gitmodules` exists | A "within this line's indented block" scope for `matchLines`. Relevance is already `relevantWhen.pathExists`. This is a new scanning primitive rather than a key — sized accordingly, and it would also unlock part of `gha/secrets-in-job-if`. |
| `sw/site-config` (`packs/static-website/site-config.mjs`) | `.github/site.config`'s five required keys, no unknown keys, every published path present | `checkKeyValueFile` already covers the key half. The remainder needs paths **derived from values** (class D below) and the `NEVER_PUBLISHED` floor. Partial conversion only — and see the class E caveat: the key list and parser are imported from the vendored action, so a declaration would fork them. |

Suggested slicing, cheapest first: (1) `product-wiki-layout`'s path half, no engine change; (2) `requireValueInArray` + `core-declared`; (3) the content-predicate quantifier + `home-seeded-packs-declared` and `cer/privacy-permission-alignment`, which share it; (4) `andPreviousLineMatches` + the macOS rule; (5) the block-scope primitive, judged on its own merits.

Each conversion must be authored red-first against the existing rule's own test fixtures, and the coded module deleted in the same commit — the pattern #839 used for the five `jwt` rules.

## B — the surface is not a file (16)

No key fixes these; the evidence does not live in the tree.

**Conversation transcript** — `comment-classification`, `feature-requirements-first`.

**Git history / the branch diff** — `task-lifecycle`, `squash-merge-history`, `reference-integrity` (dangling refs are scoped to paths *this branch deletes*), `node/earn-each-dependency`, `cer/permission-added-store-issue` (permission *sets* compared against the base, deliberately not the text diff — appending a JSON array element re-touches the prior line), `google-client-id-single-origin`, `growth-write-scope`, `dedup-prune-integrity`, `consumer-safe-change`, `engine-release-record`.

**Normalized config object / discovered packs** — `barrier` (edges come from the repo's own `config.rules`; `forbidReferences` can only carry edges written in the declaration, which is exactly why the config rule survived #838's barriers rephrase), `growth-config`, `preferences-store-configured`, `fleet-pack-seed-agrees`, `interview-answer-stale`, `adoption-answers-pending`.

The three JSON base-vs-head rules here are the ones #838's `work.addedKeys(file, atPath)` bullet is about. That helper is worth having, but it makes them *shorter coded rules*, not declared ones — worth stating plainly so the bullet is not read as a conversion.

## C — needs a real parser; a line regex is the failure mode the rule exists to avoid (12)

`content-script-module-syntax`, `declarative-content-set-icon`, `leaflet/asset-integrity`, `leaflet/tile-attribution`, `signal-teardown-routing`, `gha/secrets-in-job-if`, `gha/run-pipefail`, `aws-sam/handler-path`, `conformance-workflow`, `python-optional-import-top-level`, `python-optional-import-install-hint`, `pack-discovery-entry-await`.

Each of these carries a "PARSED, NOT GREPPED" header naming the false positives the regex version produces — `grep attribution` is satisfied by the word appearing anywhere and cannot say *which* `tileLayer` lacks it; `^import` in `packs/` flags a correct codebase; `chrome.action.setIcon({path})` is the *correct* use of a differently-cased API. Converting them ships the check they were written to replace.

Two need parsers the engine does not have at all: the python pair needs TOML (`[project.optional-dependencies]` is the only place a package is *declared* optional), and `pack-discovery-entry-await` walks the static import graph from the real manifests.

`conformance-workflow` is the near-miss in this class — `repoWide`'s `unlessSomeFileMatches` expresses "unless some workflow runs the sweep", but the trap it exists for is the *path-filtered* flow, and telling a trigger-level `paths:` from a job-level key requires the `on:`-block scoping the rule does by hand.

## D — the scan set or key set is derived from another file's data (9)

The engine picks files by path pattern or exact path. These pick them by content read elsewhere, which is precisely what makes them false-positive-free.

`web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker` (only the file an MV3 manifest names as `background.service_worker`, and only when it is authored source rather than a bundle), `firebase/functions-node-pin` and `firebase/functions-predeploy-build` (each codebase's `source` in `firebase.json` locates the `package.json`), `pack-no-enforcement-narration` (scans exactly the file each `pack.mjs` declares as `prose`), `skill-no-enforcement-narration` (fixed glob, but the forbidden-token list is the live rule-id set), `routine-structure`, `task-declaration-matches-folder` (declared `id` must equal its own directory name), `rules-index-current`, `markdown-link-labels` and `file-placement` (both resolve relative paths and compare — the second literally computes a distance).

A general `filesNamedByField` selector would unlock the firebase pair and the two manifest-driven ones. It is a bigger idea than the class-A keys and should be its own issue if wanted; noting it here so it is not lost.

## E — the check imports the definition it guards (10)

Converting these creates the second copy that `shared-constants` exists to forbid: the check would agree with a frozen snapshot instead of with the live code.

`task-declaration-shape` (enum lists imported from `engine/scheduler/slots.mjs`, `model-map.mjs`, `task-contract.mjs`), `sw/version-scheme` (`VERSION_RE` from the bump action), `sw/site-config` and `sw/release-workflows` (the same `parseConfig` the vendored action runs), `cer/release-workflows` (plus a *time-dependent* migration-tolerance window, undeclarable by construction), `preferences-store-file-names` (`isUsableIdentity` from the reader, so the check can never be stricter or looser than what actually opens the file), `shared-constants` itself (per-repo config), `declared-check-messages` (the meta-check over declaration files — it walks their spec trees), and the barrier factories in `packs/barriers/contributed.mjs`, which mint rules at runtime from whichever packs are active.

## The conclusion worth keeping

The honest backlog is **7**, not 54. The other 47 are not unconverted prose-to-checks debt — and for class E specifically, coded is the *stronger* rung, not the weaker one, because a declaration would necessarily duplicate the truth it is checking. Any future "convert the remaining imperative checks" framing should point here rather than assume the residue is inertia.

## Housekeeping spotted while counting

#838's unchecked bullet — *"Add `unlessPreviousLineMatches`, `maxLineLength`, `andLineMatches`; convert `warning-suppression`, `rules-line-length`, `task-phase-discipline`"* — has in fact landed: all three keys are in the `pattern-rules.mjs` vocabulary and all three rules now sit in `declared-checks.json`. Worth ticking there.

## Checklist

- [ ] `product-wiki-layout`: move the path half to `declared-checks.json`, keep `configGuard` coded
- [ ] `requireValueInArray` key + convert `core-declared`
- [ ] content-predicate quantifier on `requireIndexCoverage` + convert `home-seeded-packs-declared`
- [ ] value-quantifier over a parsed array + convert `cer/privacy-permission-alignment`
- [ ] `andPreviousLineMatches` key + convert `sudden-termination-vs-teardown`
- [ ] decide on the block-scope scanning primitive (`gha/checkout-submodules`, partial `gha/secrets-in-job-if`)
- [ ] tick the landed slice on #838

Every item: author the declaration red-first against the coded rule's existing fixtures, watch it fire, then delete the coded module in the same commit. `packs/README.md`'s corpus tally and the owning pack's catalog row both move on each one — recompute, never hand-increment.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/880","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-15T22:40:52Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T22:40:52Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":875,"title":"SessionStart: the selftest reports state a later step in the same firing repairs, and the preferences facet counts bullets rather than context cost","body":"Two session-start defects, both observed live in a resume of this repo on 2026-08-15.

## 1. The selftest judges a tree that has not converged yet

`engine/hooks/session-start-command.sh` runs `selftest` first, then `mount-skills` two steps later. But `mount-skills` is precisely what repairs the thing `probeSkillLinks` judges — so on any firing where the mounts are stale (a resume after the corpus moved, a fresh checkout), the selftest reports dangling links that the *same firing* fixes a second later.

Measured this session: the injected report named `adopt-claudinite` and `adopt-pack` as dangling; both links were rebuilt at `10:06:25` by the `mount-skills` step of that same run and resolve fine. The person reading the session opener is handed a finding about a state that no longer exists, with a "fix: re-run the skill mount" remedy that already ran.

The invariant that was missing: **a probe must judge state that no later step in the same firing changes.** `skill-links` is the only probe with that property today (nothing else in the sequence converges what a probe reads), so ordering is the whole fix.

## 2. The preferences facet is stated in rules, the summary in tokens

The session opener reads `… 16,500 rule tokens, 19 available skills, 9 personal preference rules.` — the corpus weight in the unit of the cost it imposes, and the preferences in a unit that says nothing about it. Preferences land in the same context window and should be reported the same way.

The token estimator (words ÷ 0.75, rounded) currently lives as two private constants in `engine/pack_loader/session-summary.mjs`; a second caller means it has to become a shared reference rather than a copied ratio.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The selftest observes the mounted skill links *after* the mount step has run, proven by a test that fails on the old order.
- [ ] The preferences facet states an estimated token count.
- [ ] One definition of the words→tokens ratio, imported by both callers.

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work (an engine release, pack updates, an extension release, research/extract material) to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

**What is already proven before step 1:** the simulator (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`, in CI) rehearses every scenario in SCENARIOS.md, including the spec bugs it caught (F13, F14, the S28 stamped-wake precision). The coverage map in `sim/README.md` names exactly what only live traffic can prove — the burst below exists to cover precisely those rows.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL (an issue showing the full lifecycle) appended beside it.

---

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

One PR containing everything, because the safety is the config flag and the disjoint issue families (`[claudinite-task]` vs `[claudinite-work]`), not PR granularity — rollback at any moment before Step 3 is a one-line config edit back to `"slots"`, with each mechanism's open items invisible to the other (proven: S29).

- [x] Label vocabulary (`task:*`, `origin:schedule`, `outcome:*`) — create-if-missing wiring
- [x] Tick workflow: cron at the hashed minute **plus `workflow_dispatch`** (the never-wait-for-the-cron lever the burst depends on)
- [x] Executor workflow: post-tick drain + `labeled`-event runs, `required_secrets` and endpoint tokens stamped into its env (DESIGN §14 secrets path)
- [x] Janitor re-target: executing-leash on the tick, agent leash, stale-ready, stuck-dependency sweep (F14)
- [x] Dependency fields, the `after` pick-time yield, `create-work-item` + the wake/re-queue lever
- [x] F8: signal collectors' self-trigger exclusions learn the new vocabulary **in this PR**, before any repo flips
- [x] `taskScheduler.dispatch: "queue"` **on canon, in this same PR**; slot machinery stays in the tree, dormant on canon, live everywhere else
- [x] Gate green: full suite (sim included) + conformance sweep
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (same afternoon, zero approvals)

Fire the tick by `workflow_dispatch`, then drive **real work** through every live-only path. Each row's acceptance is an issue URL showing the full lifecycle on one item. Any row red = fix on canon (flag still reversible) and re-run that row — the burst is idempotent because forcing is idempotent.

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** dispatched tick creates every task's item `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor — the issue list is the dashboard — [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771), 12 items #860–#870
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** wake a task with no work: one ask, roll to tomorrow, reason visible — #860
- [ ] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** touch a stale issue, wake `tidy-issues`: claim comment → prework → hand-off → live session → `outcome:done` + exec record
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [ ] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** cut an engine release (real baselining work) and stage extract material; wake `baselining`, watch `growth-extract` yield then run the same hour
- [ ] **B6 hourly cadence (S22):** file a real extractor request, watch `create-extractor` catch it within the hour; otherwise its hourly roll is the evidence
- [ ] **B7 missing-secret posture + re-queue (§14 step 7, F7, S19):** point a scratch task at an endpoint whose secret is deliberately unset: hand-off converges `needs-human` naming it; set the secret, re-queue, watch it converge
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [ ] All burst rows green

## Step 3 — PR‑2: fleet flip + slot machinery deletion (approval №2)

- [ ] Engine release carrying the migration note: flip `dispatch` to `"queue"`; nothing to relabel (disjoint families — old open dispatch issues are drained by a human or closed obsolete, finite and visible)
- [ ] **Slot machinery deleted in this same PR** (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks) — the no-lingering-legacy discipline
- [ ] The pack update flow stages only `pendingSchedulerWorkflow`, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reaches no member — add it to the staged set in this PR's engine release
- [ ] **Approval №2: PR‑2 merged + engine release cut**
- [ ] Every member's baselining forced (the old mechanism's last act converges the new wiring) — no waiting for nightlies
- [ ] Per-member mini-burst (B1–B3 via each repo's dispatched tick) green for every member
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member "flipped and burst-verified" fan-out items + a fan-in status item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

Rollback after PR‑2 is `git revert` of PR‑2 (the flag alone no longer suffices once slot code is deleted) — accepted, because Step 2 already proved the end state on canon before any member moved.

## Done means

- [ ] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [ ] All members flipped; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

Flipping a member without that gives it a tick with no label-event executor and no secrets env: the drain still runs it hourly, so nothing is silently dead, but the latency and the secrets both regress. Two changes to the design landed inside PR‑1 and are worth naming here, because both simplify what Step 2 has to prove:

- **Invocation is a routine's API trigger**, verified against the routines docs rather than assumed. Firing a routine runs *its stored prompt*, and our `text` arrives wrapped as untrusted — so the payload names the item and the nonce and instructs nothing, and the session's instructions are a tracked file (`engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md`) that the routine's one-line prompt points at.
- **One call per item, never retried** (owner correction) — which deleted the agent-side claim protocol rather than simplifying it. There is no idempotency key on the endpoint, so a retry is precisely how two sessions land on one item. An unanswered call now leaves the item with the agent, and the janitor's agent leash settles it either way. `MAX_HANDOFF_ATTEMPTS`, the attempt counter and the bounded revert are all gone.

{"number":855,"title":"Where CI time goes: the fixture-signing cost, and a weekly task that keeps measuring","body":"A full breakdown of this repo's CI, the fleet-wide surface, and the standing mechanism so this does not need re-deriving by hand.

**Breakdown (CI, per step).** Job ~60s: checkout 3–5s, setup-node 5s, **unit tests 48s**, conformance sweep 1–2s, gates ~0s. Only the test step is worth profiling.

**The dominant local cost is not in CI.** `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s `makeRepo` pins identity and auto-gc but not `commit.gpgsign`, so in a session with signing configured every fixture commit is a round trip to a signing service: **202ms per fixture against 38ms without**. Local suite 71s → 52s with it off. Runners have no signing configured, so CI never paid it — which is exactly why the earlier local numbers overstated the CI win. This repo's local pack already carried the lesson (with the descriptor-leak failure mode) and it was never applied to the helper.

**Fleet-wide surface is already fast.** What every member runs: work-scope check 235ms, world sweep ~800ms of which only 88ms is rule execution (37 rules; slowest is `pack-discovery-entry-await` at 63ms), `discoverPacks` 58ms, `buildContext` 41ms. Nothing to win here; recording the numbers so it is not re-profiled.

**Longest file, and a negative result.** Under CI-like conditions the serial total is 146s across 142 files, and `packs-tests/rehearsal/rehearsal.test.mjs` is 27.6s of it — 19%, 4x the next file. Its 25 cases are independent, but running them concurrently moved the file only 27.6s → 25s and the **whole suite not at all** (51s both arms, twice each): once signing is out of the way the suite is CPU-bound on 4 cores. Not shipping that.

**Distribution.** Not a few slow tests — 583 tests sat in the 200ms–1s band, which is the signature of a fixed per-test fixture cost rather than slow cases.

Landing: the helper fix with a test that forces a hostile ambient config (so it means something on a runner too), the lesson promoted from this repo's local pack to `basics/writing-tests` where every member gets it, a `ci-performance-evaluation` skill recording the method, and a weekly `basics/ci-performance` task that measures each workflow's median against the previous window and only spends an agent on a real regression.

{"number":590,"title":"Adoption never sets the two repo settings baselining depends on — add them to bootstrap (both are scriptable)","body":"Baselining's delivery depends on two repository settings that **nothing in adoption ever sets, checks, or mentions**. `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md` has zero references to either — the only mentions anywhere in the corpus are the error strings added by #585.

Both are the direct cause of the two-day fleet stall.

## The settings

| Setting | UI | API |
|---|---|---|
| Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests | Settings → Actions → General | `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow` → `{"can_approve_pull_request_reviews": true}` |
| Allow auto-merge | Settings → General → Pull Requests | `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` → `{"allow_auto_merge": true}` |

**Both are readable and writable by script** — plain REST, no UI-only step. The matching `GET` on each returns the current value, so a conformance check could assert them rather than only bootstrap setting them.

The constraint is the credential, not the API: both require **admin** on the repo. The Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do it, so this cannot be self-healed by baselining from inside the member. It belongs to either:

- **adoption** (`adopt-claudinite`), which already runs in a session with the owner's own credentials, or
- **the sheepdog pack**, whose `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` spans the account — it could converge both settings fleet-wide alongside `fleet-freshness`, and would catch a repo whose settings were later flipped back.

The second is the stronger option: adoption sets it once, whereas the sheepdog sweep keeps it true.

## Why it matters

Without the first, the maintenance PR is never created (#585 — silent before that fix, loud after). Without the second, an `auto-merge` member's PR opens and never lands. Neither is visible from inside the member repo, and neither produced any signal until it was investigated by hand.

## Suggested scope

1. Adoption sets both over the owner's credentials, and records what it set.
2. A check (or the sheepdog freshness sweep) asserts both remain true, reporting the exact API path when they are not.
3. `adopt-claudinite` documents them, so a hand-adopted repo does not silently miss them.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/590","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-30T21:42:38Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T04:21:57Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":381,"title":"Restructure the tree so the engine and content copy as clean folders (engine/, engine-tests/, packs-tests/, skills-tests/)","body":"Restructure the repo so each copyable unit is one clean folder:

- **`engine/`** — the whole engine in one folder, copyable without tests: `engine/checks/` (runner, lib, Stop hook, PreToolUse guard), `engine/mount/` (vendor writer, session-start orchestrator, sync/env-setup scripts), and the pack/skill machinery moved off the content roots into `engine/packs/` (registry, load-active-prose, env, interview) and `engine/skills/` (registry, mount-skills).
- **`engine-tests/`** — mirrors the engine's subfolders (`checks/`, `mount/`, `packs/`, `skills/`), absorbing the former `checks/test/` and the in-tree `*.test.mjs`.

{"number":803,"title":"Every dispatch starts two executor sessions; one burns a container to stand down","body":"**Corrected.** I filed this claiming the claim protocol is not exclusive. That was wrong, and the correction matters because the original framing would have sent someone to fix something that already works.

`engine/scheduler/executor.md` step 2 already specifies read → swap → **re-read**, with earliest-claim-wins and an explicit "end the session without dispatching" for the loser. On the observed run the protocol did exactly that: two claims, one delivery commit, PR merged once. What I saw was the guard working.

## The real issue: the duplicate firing itself

Two sessions still start for one dispatch. `ClaudiniteCanary#62`:

```
Claimed by executor session (Claude Code, session f29055ea-…) at 2026-08-13T19:24:34Z.
Claimed by executor session `91596dae-…`               at 2026-08-13T19:24:38Z.
```

`fileHandoff` creates the issue with **both** labels in a single POST (`labels: [readyLabel, escalation.name]`), so this is not two label-add calls from our side. GitHub emits a `labeled` event per label on creation, so a routine triggering on `labeled` fires twice.

That costs a whole container and model session per dispatch to do nothing but read labels and quit, on **every** escalated dispatch across the fleet. It also leaves a stray claim comment on every such issue, which is what made me misread the protocol in the first place — the artifact of a correctly-handled race is indistinguishable at a glance from a race that wasn't handled.

## Worth fixing, in order of cheapness

1. **File the issue with the ready label only**, and add the escalation label in a follow-up call *after* creation. One `labeled` event at create → one firing. The escalation label stays countable. (Check that the follow-up add doesn't itself re-fire the routine — if it does, this doesn't help and the fix is 2 or 3.)
2. **Have the routine trigger on `opened` rather than `labeled`**, filtered by label. Lives in the CCR routine config, outside this repo.
3. **Have the losing session delete its own claim comment** before standing down, so a handled race leaves no trace. Cosmetic, but it removes the misreading this issue is evidence of.

## Also observed

The two claim comments use different wording — one names "(Claude Code, session …)", the other backticks the id alone. That suggests the two sessions were running different vendored generations of `executor.md`, which is worth understanding independently: the routine's two firings may not be picking up the same instructions.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/803","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"comments":3,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-13T19:32:27Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T04:21:36Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

Investigated. Three findings, one of which corrects the issue.

**"Also observed" is wrong — the two sessions ran the same instructions.** `executor.md` step 2.2 says only "post a claim comment naming this session and the UTC time"; it gives no template, so the wording is free-form model prose and two sessions on identical instructions will naturally differ. Independently: the fleet routine's sources do not include ClaudiniteCanary, and there is exactly one `Claudinite executor - ClaudiniteCanary` routine. Both sessions came from that one routine. There is no vendored-generation skew to understand.

**Option 3 is not implementable as written.** The executor session is MCP-only, and the GitHub MCP server exposes no delete-comment or edit-comment tool — `add_issue_comment` is the whole surface. The loser cannot withdraw its claim. #811 does the reachable version: it states the stand-down on the issue, so the artifact reads unambiguously as a handled race, and unlike deletion it leaves the duplicate countable while the duplicate is still unfixed.

**Option 1 looks ineffective, and the reason is the observation itself.** If the routine matched on the *added* label name, a create with two labels would match once and one session would start. Two started. So the routine is firing on something broader — the issue carrying the ready label whatever the event, or `opened` and `labeled` both. Under either, adding the escalation label in a follow-up call still fires it a second time, and the extra POST buys nothing.

I can't settle which, because the firing rule lives in the CCR routine config and `list_triggers` returns the launcher prompt, model and sources but no event or label filter. What settles it: file a dispatch-shaped issue with the ready label only and count the sessions. One → the trigger is `labeled`-with-a-broad-filter and option 1 is worth doing; two → it also fires on `opened` and only option 2 (trigger on `opened`, filtered by label) fixes it. That's a live firing of a real executor, so it's yours to run rather than mine.

One option the list doesn't have, cheapest of all if you'll take the trade: **drop the escalation label and count the code off the dispatch body**, which already carries it (`run.mjs` passes `reason` into `dispatchBody`). One label at creation is one event under every hypothesis above. The cost is that the condition stops being countable by label search, which is the reason you added it — your call, not mine.

Worth noting on urgency: this costs one wasted container per *escalated* dispatch, not per dispatch — an unescalated one is filed with a single label. The loser exits at step 2.3 without writing, so the waste is bounded and nothing runs twice. And `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` replaces this trigger path wholesale; option 2's config change may be work you do once and then discard.

# Extract lessons from a conversation

The **dialogue** half of lesson extraction: read one agent ↔ user session — its turns *and* the actions
taken in it — and convert its friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less
dependent on human steering. Its sibling [extract-from-activity](../extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) mines
what the work committed; this one mines how the work went.

The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
surface lives stay canonical in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't
re-derive it. What follows is only what reading a *conversation* adds.

## The goal

Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less rework, less
waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but as "where did this
cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost next time." If a pass can't name
a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's fine.

## Where the conversation comes from

- **A captured log** on the repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch (`<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`),
  read with plain git in the checkout — `git show origin/conversation-logs:<file>`. The log carries
  per-entry timestamps, per-message token usage, and the `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs behind every
  wall-time number, which is exactly what the measured analysis below needs. This is the routine path.
- **The live session**, when an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective. Same method; deliver the
  capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**, never one that self-merges.

**Never reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner decides
when a session is done enough to mine.

## What to look for — the friction signals

Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop cost more than
necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.

### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user

The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I meant…"); the agent
building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose
answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.

**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every question the
user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate **convention or glossary entry**;
a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc
the agent reads cold and gets right the first time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds
correctly **without the round-trip**.

### 2. Suboptimal agent actions

The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran a command
that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light one fit; reinvented
something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written to "verify"; missed an existing
convention and had it corrected in review.

**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing helper/convention
so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read** (the usage-site-vs-central call is in
[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). The test: next time the agent takes the good path
first, not after a detour.

### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them

The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been parallel; a
padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its result was already in
hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already green.

**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers from the log's own timestamps
and separate the kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting**
(sleeps, polling, a finished process not yet killed). The numbers are computable, never estimated. A fix is
only credible against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
was already optimal.

**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the subject of
the standing **efficiency analysis** in [the unattended-agents skill](../unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold
a wall-time finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
loss of quality.

## Encode the questions the user keeps asking

The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks *repeatedly* are a
checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how many processes ran — could it be
fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its work was done?", stop waiting to be asked —
fold those exact questions into a **standing self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the
relevant work, and close with a terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each
recurring question converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively, with numbers.

## Two passes per log, and the second one may overturn the first

A captured log gets a **fresh pass** within a day of capture and a **final hindsight pass** just before
retention deletes it, against the corpus as it stands by then. The hindsight pass is a real re-read, not a
formality: a friction signal that looked situational the first time may have recurred since, and a lesson
landed since may have made a keeper redundant. Both directions are legitimate outcomes.

## Provenance: summarize the exchange, never paste it

For each rule that actually **lands** from a log, post one short comment on the issue the log names
(`--issue-<n>--` in its filename; **`--issue-0--` means the capture had no associated issue**, so there is
nothing to post on and the rule simply lands without a comment):

- one provenance line — the rule added, the capture date, the session id;
- then a **200-word-max** description of just the slice of conversation that caused the rule: what was
  asked, what went wrong or got corrected, and why the rule follows from it.

**Summarize, never transcribe.** The dialogue itself is far too verbose for an issue — no pasted turns
beyond a short quoted phrase, never raw JSONL, never a rendered transcript. A log that yields nothing gets
**no** comment: extraction is the only path to permanence, and a log's conversation is gone once retention
deletes it. That is a deliberate call, so a padded "lesson" written to feel productive costs more than the
silence it replaced.

1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	**First check whether a canon pack already owns it, from the catalog and not from the mount.** A repo
42	holds only the packs it *declares*, so "nothing here covers this" is a fact about the mount rather than
43	about the corpus — and acting on it homes the lesson locally in territory a canon pack already owns.
44	Read `.claudinite/shared/packs/directory.GENERATED.md` (canon-side `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`),
45	which states every canon pack's boundary including the ones this repo doesn't hold. Where the owning
46	pack's stated territory is merely too narrow, propose widening it rather than routing around it.
47	
48	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
49	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
50	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
51	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
52	
53	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
54	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits, the lesson lands in the repo's general local pack. A **new** local
55	pack is justified only by the repo's own **project structure** — a segment of the repo's tree whose work is
56	its own territory (a `client` pack for work under `client/`), so a repo's local packs mirror its layout.
57	**Never mint a local pack around a technology or a methodology**, however real the knowledge: capture those
58	lessons in the structural pack that owns the work, and let the canon-side promote stage — Claudinite's call,
59	never a member's — decide whether a technology or methodology facet earns a pack of its own.
60	
61	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
62	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
63	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
64	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
65	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
66	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
67	
68	**Two kinds never become a pack rule, however strong the evidence** — filter on what the lesson is *about*
69	before picking a mechanism. (1) **The owner's own preferences** — which word authorizes a merge, tone, how a
70	summary is shaped. They belong to the person, are injected per session from their own preference file, and
71	change without any repo hearing about it; a pack copy goes stale silently and then contradicts the live one.
72	(2) **The agent framework's own loading mechanics** — which packs are declared, why a skill didn't mount, why
73	an injection missed. That's engine plumbing, not project knowledge: a real defect there is filed upstream, and
74	writing it down as a project rule preserves the bug instead of fixing it.
75	
76	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
77	
78	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
79	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
80	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
81	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.

## PR #881 — Replace an item body's section rather than appending a second one

What it did: fixed `withSection` so hand-off replaces a same-named section in place instead of appending a duplicate (e.g., a queue item ending up with two `### Context` sections).

No review discussion (0 review comments, 0 issue comments) — solo-merged.

Candidate lesson: The bug was invisible to unit tests because "every unit test of `withSection` passed, because each tested one call" — the defect only appears when the function is applied **more than once over an object's lifecycle** (hand-off, then a re-queue running hand-off again). `rollBody` had already hand-worked-around the same bug at one call site without anyone generalizing it ("the tell that the append-only behaviour was known; it just never generalized"). Durable rule candidate: *for any function that mutates a document/body repeatedly across its lifecycle, a per-call unit test is insufficient — write a round-trip/idempotency test (apply twice, assert no duplication) before trusting single-call tests.* This is a reasonably new, generalizable testing lesson, not just an implementation detail.

## PR #874 — Stage the executor workflow beside the tick, in one cycle

What it did: extended the pack-update flow to also deliver `claudinite-executor.yml` for queue-dispatch members, alongside the existing scheduler-workflow staging, so the two converge in the same cycle.

No review discussion at all (0/0). The PR body itself already explains the "silent generator-with-no-worker" failure mode and why it's additive rather than folded into the existing lane — but this is authorial rationale, not a review-surfaced correction, and the "looks-healthy-but-is-dead" class it describes is explicitly named as the same class #797 already covers. Nothing new/durable found beyond what's presumably already in corpus.

## PR #854 — The work-item queue: the whole mechanism, canon flipped

What it did: landed the entire queue-dispatch mechanism (tick/executor/janitor/invoke) behind a config flag, flipping canon's own dispatch to `queue`.

No PR-level review comments, but the **commit history itself carries an owner correction mid-flight** — this is the richest finding of the four:
- Commit 1 built invocation assuming at-least-once delivery, with an agent-side claim/lease protocol to arbitrate duplicate calls from client-side retries on timeout.
- Commit 3 message: *"Owner correction: the API should be called once per item. It is right, and it removes a whole protocol rather than simplifying one."* Reasoning quoted in the commit: *"a retry is only safe when you know the first call did nothing, and the timeout is exactly the case where you cannot."* The fix replaced retry+dedup with at-most-once invocation and three outcomes (refused / unanswered-stays-with-agent / normal), letting existing janitor sweep rules (agent leash) settle the unanswered case instead of a bespoke claim arbiter.

Candidate lesson (strong, new): *When a call's failure mode includes "timeout, and I cannot know whether the callee actually ran" — the corpus's existing "unknown is a state of its own" rule is adjacent but doesn't cover this — building a retry-plus-deduplication protocol to paper over that uncertainty is often the wrong shape entirely; prefer declining to retry (at-most-once) and letting an existing timeout/reaper mechanism resolve the unanswered case, rather than inventing a new claim/lease layer whose only job is to arbitrate a retry you didn't need to make.* This is a genuine mid-flight redesign (a whole protocol deleted, not merely tuned) driven by an explicit owner correction, and it reads as durable engineering guidance beyond "verify against docs" (which is a separate, already-covered lesson from commit 2's "comment-shaped guess would have shipped wrong").

Also on this PR: the merge commit (`c8a3cc28`) resolving a conflict with #858 dropped a newly-added `file-placement` acceptance entry rather than reapplying it, correctly following #858's just-landed policy — minor, not independently new.

## PR #858 — file-placement is advisory only — no acceptance entries

What it did: removed the "or accept it in `.claudinite-checks.json`" language from the `file-placement` check's remedy text and deleted all nine existing acceptance entries for it, since the check is (and always was) advisory-only and never blocked a run.

No review discussion; driven by an owner-filed issue (#856), not a review back-and-forth. Issue text: *"That is cost with no purchase. An acceptance entry exists to make a blocking violation reviewable; on an advisory finding it buys nothing and taxes every repo that hits the smell."*

Candidate lesson (moderate, plausibly new): *A check's own remedy/`fix` text is part of its contract and can override its declared severity in practice — an advisory check whose fix text names a config-acceptance escape hatch will be treated as a demanded gate by sessions acting on it, even though nothing enforces it.* Generalizable rule: when authoring a check's failure/fix message, never suggest a config-acceptance remedy unless the check's severity is actually blocking. Worth flagging as a candidate for the checks-authoring guidance, distinct from anything about `file-placement` specifically.

## Part A — PRs #878, #857, #853

All three are open (not merged), have **zero comments and zero reviews** — they were "touched" only via being opened/updated with commits, not discussed. No review-thread lessons to report for any of them.

- **#878** — "Converge before reporting at session start, and weigh preferences in tokens." Fixes #875. Reorders `mount-skills` before `selftest` in the SessionStart hook (a probe must judge state no later step in the same firing changes) and switches the preferences facet from bullet-count to a shared token estimator. Clean, self-contained, tests-first per its own description.
- **#857** — "Where CI time goes." Fixes #855. Diagnoses/fixes unsigned-fixture-commit cost in `makeRepo` (202ms vs 38ms per commit — CI runners never paid it, so it explains a prior local/CI discrepancy), adds a `ci-performance-evaluation` skill and a weekly `basics/ci-performance` task. Notably reverts two things it tried and rejected in the same PR (promoting the fixture-signing lesson to a portable pack — wrong, it's Claudinite-only test infra; and parallelizing the slowest test file — file-level win didn't move the CPU-bound suite total).
- **#853** — "Promote eight fleet lessons into the canon." Growth-promote batch pulling lessons from ClaudiniteWebsite/EdFringeNow/MissingBulbWebsite/Sheepdog into canon prose (git-github-advanced, basics, authoring-agent-docs, etc.), all folds/additions, none converted to checks (all judgment/in-flight-behavior). Not auto-merged by design.

No durable-lesson-bearing discussion in any of these three — they're solo authored PRs awaiting review, useful only as pointers to what already landed in RULES.md (which the corpus already captures).

Routine (status/triage comments only, no new lesson): **#334** (doc-target confusion self-corrected across two triage passes — DESIGN.md moved/renamed, resolved within thread), **#766** (mechanical line-wrap progress tracking), **#230** (Node 20→24 bump, repeatedly re-scoped as workflow files got renamed/removed across sessions — pure status), **#381** (restructure tracked via repeated "needs-decision" status checks, structural convention already shipped differently than issue asked), **#590** (quick-win scoping, no new content), **#875** (verification comment only — not yet landed), **#876** (fresh issue, no comments), **#880** (fresh issue, no comments).

Contains an actual finding/decision worth flagging:

- **#882** — New issue: queue-mode agentic sessions print `claudinite-task-exec … [unknown]` because `instructions.md` never tells the session what replaces the old slot-id join key (should be the issue number, e.g. `[#867]`). This is a real, freshly-discovered gap in the new tasks-dispatch mechanism — not yet a "lesson" per se (it's a bug report on brand-new machinery, still open), but worth downstream awareness since it's about to be fixed.
- **#170** — Comment is itself a self-triage flagging that the issue's own "Action" (periodic manual check of release notes) **conflicts with the standing basics rule** ("never a human's memory — make the follow-up a mechanism that comes to you"). This is the corpus rule already stated being applied/enforced, not a new lesson — correctly identifies but doesn't add anything new.
- **#239** — Triage comment corrected an *earlier* triage comment in the same thread: first pass claimed `bootstrap.md` still had manual relocation steps; the follow-up re-checked and found that section gone too, narrowing scope to one surviving item. Shows the pattern "verify-before-trusting-prior-comment" but this is existing practice (the "correcting/auditing an artifact" and "derive from source" rules already in basics), not new.
- **#877** — Owner naming rule stated directly in the issue body (design-review session, 2026-08-15): "prefer spelled-out names that read without contextual knowledge — single nouns like 'tick' fail that test." This reads as a fresh, explicit owner ruling on naming, somewhat narrower than but adjacent to the existing basics rule "name it for its scope/responsibility, not the technology or mechanism." Possibly worth a light note/example addition rather than a new rule — low novelty, high specificity.
- **#801** — The tasks-dispatch migration tracking issue, very active (7 comments this window), documents live burst-testing findings: two real defects only found via real traffic (#879/#881 double-Context-section bug, and #882 above), a "one call per item, never retried" design correction (no idempotency key — a retry would double-claim), and confirms `labeled`-event latency ~2s. These are already being captured as their own issues/PRs (#879, #882) — the pattern "real traffic surfaces defects rehearsal can't" is already a canon lesson (writing-tests / bug-investigation), so nothing new to extract beyond what's already flowing into #882.
- **#803** — Multi-comment investigation thread. The issue itself opens with an explicit self-correction ("I filed this claiming X, that was wrong") — the filer initially misread a correctly-handled race as a broken one because "the artifact of a correctly-handled race is indistinguishable at a glance from a race that wasn't handled." Latest (2026-08-15) triage comment just re-confirms quick-win scope, no new content. The self-correction pattern is a mildly interesting instance but is really just an application of "verify against source before trusting a symptom" — already covered.
- **#855** — Duplicate/companion of #857 (same underlying investigation, different issue number); no comments, closed by #857.

**Bottom line**: Nothing in this window clears the bar for a genuinely new durable lesson beyond what's already in the corpus or already being captured by open follow-up issues (#882 fix, #877 naming note). The strongest candidate for extraction, if anything, is #877's explicit owner naming ruling (single-noun names failing the "reads without contextual knowledge" test) — worth a light sharpening of the existing naming-a-symbol rule, not a new entry.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmi
